title:
Comment of Karen Murdock in Docket(s)/Project(s) P-15423-000
Submission Date: 10/25/2026

documents.name: 151839.txt
documents.text:
Karen Murdock, Homer, AK.
My name is Karen Murdock. I reside at 55200 East End Road, Homer. I am submitting the following as public comments.

I am quite concerned about the permit application made by the  DeepGreen Cook Inlet LLC to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) for a hyperscale data center underwater in the Cook Inlet Forelands region offshore of Nikiski.  This underwater data center could have many serious impacts on marine life, local utility ratepayers and the entire ecosystem of Cook Inlet.


A hyper scale underwater data center in the Cook Inlet Forelands area would endanger our fisheries by releasing toxic copper directly into the habitat of our Cook Inlet salmon population.  This would have a tremendous impact on all of us who depend on our salmon for commercial/ personal/sport/subsistence use.  This would drastically affect jobs and our food source. The increased water temperature caused by the data center’s discharge of waste heat has a grave potential to significantly harm salmon and the entire ecosystem of Cook Inlet.  Our salmon is our precious commodity and needs to be protected.  Please protect our marine life by submitting comments to the FERC against the approval of the DeepGreen Cook Inlet underwater data center permit.  

There are many other concerns that this underwater data center could have on the Cook Inlet. The significant noise generated by the data center would impact the migration of the endangered Beluga whales blocking their feeding and calving grounds.   The energy used by the data center during slack tide would  impact HEA consumers.  Our HEA current rates are presenting hardships for many in the Borough.  A substantial increase would be staggering. 
 
As a resident of the Kenai Peninsula Borough since 1979, I have personal use and subsistence fished for decades, providing my family with nutritious salmon for a healthy lifestyle.  Many of my friends have commercially fished, providing for their families.  Having lived through the Exxon Valdez oil spill,  we have learned how fragile our waters and the ecosystems are.  Please protect the waters of Cook Inlet by denying issuance of the permit.

Thank you for this opportunity to submit my concerns.
